answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a plume as the anchor of the cost.
